violations.title: Records, Parasite Destruction by Freezing
violations.observation: No records of freezing for parasite destruction are maintained for the following raw, raw marinated, partially cooked or marinated-partially cooked fish that are served or sold in ready-to-eat form: FROZEN MARINATED RAW SOFT SHELL CRABS PACKAGE FOR RETAIL SERVICE IN 2 DOOR UPRIGHT FREEZER IN DINING AREA.

PLEASE OBTAIN CRABS FROM SUPPLIER WHICH IS COMPLIANT AND CAN PROVIDE A PARASITE DESTRUCTION LETTER. COMPLIANCE WILL BE CONFIRMED BY FOLLOW UP INSPECTION LEE HWA (Inspection Date: 07/28/2026) Page 3 of 4

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: SOYBEAN SOUP, SPICY SOYBEAN SOUP AND KIMCHI SOUP PREPARED 2 DAYS PRIOR AND KIMCHI PREPARED 1 DAY PRIOR WITHOUT APPROPRIATE DATE MARKING.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. out_items.name: Compliance with variance, specialized process, HACCP

violations.title: Variance Requirement, Health Department Determines Need
violations.observation: Specialized processing method of food preservation used for PREPARATION OF FERMENTED KIMCHI TO BE HELD FOR MORE THAN 7 DAYS.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall obtain a variance from the Regulatory Authority as specified in 8-103.10 and under 8-103.11 before: 1. smoking food as a method of food preservation rather than as a method for flavor enhancement, 2. curing food, 3. using food additives or adding components such as vinegar, 4. packaging food using a Reduced Oxygen Packaging method, 5. operating a molluscan shellfish life-support system display tank used to store and display shellfish that are offered for human consumption, 6. custom processing animals that are for personal use as food and not for sale or service in a food establishment, 7. preparing food by another method that is determined by the Regularty Authority to require a variance or, 8. sprouting seeds or beans. EDUCATION PROVIDED. KIMCHI PREPARED AND HELD FOR MORE THAN 7 DAYS WERE DISCARDED. EHS PROVIDED GUIDANCE DOCUMENTATION FOR SUBMISSION OF VARIANCE AND HACCP TO PIC AND PERSONNEL ASSIGNED TO ASSIST WITH TRANSLATION DURING INSPECTION. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO DISCONTINUE IN THE PREPARATION OF FERMENTED KIMCHI UNTIL VARIANCE WITH HACCP HAS BEEN SUBMITTED AND APPROVED BY THE HEALTH DEPARTMENT.

out_items.name: In-use utensils properly stored

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: RICE SCOOPS STORED IN WATER AT 88F.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO REMOVE UTENSILS FOR CLEANING AND SANITIZING AND REPLACE WITH SCOOPS STORED IN DRY CLEAN AND SANITIZED PAN. PLEASE ENSURE CONTINUED COMPLIANCE

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: BEEF BROTH AT 45F PREPARED THE PREVIOUS DAY IN COVERED LOWES BUCKET IN WALK IN REFRIGERATOR.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO DISCARD FOODS DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE USE ICE WANDS OR ICE BATHS, IN FREEZER TO RAPIDLY COOL FOODS. DO NOT COVER FOODS UNTIL COOLED TO 41F OR BELOW.

out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: Duty of PIC, Employee Health Policy in Place
violations.observation: Upon discussion with the person-in-charge, one or more of the elements of an effective employee health policy is either missing or incomplete. A complete employee health policy is required to be in place at the food establishment. At the time of this inspection, the Health Department provided and reviewed handouts and resource information in a red folder labeled 'Employee Health Policy.' OBSERVED NO EMPLOYEE HEALTH POLICY AT TIME OF INSPECTION.
violations.corrective_action: A complete employee health policy must have the following elements: 1) Employee training on foodborne illness, particularly symptoms of illness and prevention of the Big Six illnesses (see 'What is Foodborne Illness' handout); and 2) Documentation that employees have been instructed of their responsibility to report symptoms of, diagnosis of or exposure to foodborne illness to management (see 'Employee Illness Reporting Agreement' handout); and 3) A management plan to restrict or exclude employees, as applicable, who have symptoms, diagnosis or exposure to foodborne illness (see 'Employee Illness Decision Guide for PIC/CFM' handout). The information provided at the time of this inspection will help you develop and implement this policy. Handouts are available in the following languages: English, Arabic, Chinese (traditional), Farsi, Hindi, Korean, Spanish, Thai, Urdu and Vietnamese. If you have any questions about your employee health policy, please contact your area inspector or contact the Health Department at 703-246-2201, TTY 703-591-6435. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS PROVIDED COPY TO PIC DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE REVIEW WITH EMPLOYEES AND HAVE EACH SIGN A COPY. KEEP SIGNED COPIES ON SITE FOR REVIEW BY HEALTH DEPARTMENT.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: UTENSILS NEAR COOK LINE IN WATER AT 83F; RICE UTENSILS IN WATER AT 76F IN BACK KITCHEN.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PIC INSTRUCTED EMPLOYEE TO HEAT WATER WITH UTENSILS TO 135F AND REPLACE RICE UTENSILS AND STORE IN DRY PAN DURING INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: Duty of PIC, Employee Health Policy in Place
violations.observation: Upon discussion with the person-in-charge, one or more of the elements of an effective employee health policy is either missing or incomplete. A complete employee health policy is required to be in place at the food establishment. At the time of this inspection, the Health Department provided and reviewed handouts and resource information in a red folder labeled 'Employee Health Policy.' OBSERVED NO EMPLOYEE HEALTH POLICY ON SITE AT TIME OF INSPECTION.
violations.corrective_action: A complete employee health policy must have the following elements: 1) Employee training on foodborne illness, particularly symptoms of illness and prevention of the Big Six illnesses (see 'What is Foodborne Illness' handout); and 2) Documentation that employees have been instructed of their responsibility to report symptoms of, diagnosis of or exposure to foodborne illness to management (see 'Employee Illness Reporting Agreement' handout); and 3) A management plan to restrict or exclude employees, as applicable, who have symptoms, diagnosis or exposure to foodborne illness (see 'Employee Illness Decision Guide for PIC/CFM' handout). The information provided at the time of this inspection will help you develop and implement this policy. Handouts are available in the following languages: English, Arabic, Chinese (traditional), Farsi, Hindi, Korean, Spanish, Thai, Urdu and Vietnamese. If you have any questions about your employee health policy, please contact your area inspector or contact the Health Department at 703-246-2201, TTY 703-591-6435. EHS PROVIDED COPY TO PIC DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE MAKE COPIES AND REVIEW WITH EMPLOYEES. HAVE EACH EMPLOYEE SIGN AND MAINTAIN SIGNED COPIES ON SITE FOR REVIEW BY HEALTH DEPARTMENT. LEE HWA (Inspection Date: 02/07/2025) Page 2 of 3

out_items.name: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use

violations.title: Eating, Drinking, or Using Tobacco
violations.observation: A food employee was observed eating, smoking, or drinking in areas where they may contaminate food, clean equipment, utensils or other items needing protection. OBSERVED EMPLOYEE DRINKING FROM OPEN CONTAINER NEAR PREP TABLE IN BACK KITCHEN.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees may only eat, drink, or use tobacco in a designated area like a dining room or office area. Employees shall not eat or drink in the kitchen areas, warewashing areas, or storage areas where items may become contaminated. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PLEASE ENSURE EMPLOYEES CONTINUE TO COMPLY WITH DRINKING FROM CUPS COVERED WITH LIDS WITH STRAWS AWAY FROM FOOD PREPARATION AREAS.

out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: RAW CHICKEN ABOVE BEAN SPROUTS IN 3 DOOR PREP TOP; RAW BEEF AND CHICKEN ABOVE PREPARED CUT VEGETABLES IN M3 TURBO AIR 2 DOOR UPRIGHT UNIT; RAW SHELLED EGGS, RAW CHICKEN AND BEEF OVER PREPARED SAUCES AND VEGETABLES IN WALK IN REFRIGERATOR.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PIC REORGANIZED ALL RAW ANIMAL PROTEINS STORED ABOVE PREPARED VEGETABLES AND SAUCES DURING INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Proper date marking and disposition

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: OBSERVED VARIOUS HOME MADE SAUCES PREPARED AND HELD FOR MORE THAN 24 HOURS WITHOUT DATE MARKING.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PIC INSTRUCTED EMPLOYEES TO DATE MARK HOME MADE SAUCES DURING INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Food properly labeled, original container

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: WORKING CONTAINERS OF IN USE SALT, SUGAR, SPICES, OILS, SAUCES ON CART NEAR WOK LINE WITHOUT LABELS.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PIC INSTRUCTED EMPLOYEE TO APPLY LABELS DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE LABEL AND ENSURE CONTINUED COMPLIANCE.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. OBSERVED BEVERAGES, TEAS AND SINGLE SERVICE ITEMS STORED ON DIRECTLY ON FLOOR AND ON CRATE IN BAR AREA.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PIC RELOCATED ITEMS STORED ON FLOOR AND CRATE TO APPROVE SHELVING IN KITCHEN DURING INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Wiping cloths properly used and stored

violations.title: Wipings Clothes Stored in Sanitizer Solution
violations.observation: Wet wiping cloths used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces were observed stored on the counter: 3 DOOR PREP TOP (WOK LINE), 1 DOOR PREP TOP (FRONT SERVICE) AND BACK KITCHEN COUNTER.
violations.corrective_action: Wet wiping cloths are to be used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces and are to be held in a chemical sanitizer solution at the appropriate concentration between uses. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PIC INSTRUCTED EMPLOYEE TO PREPARE SANITIZER BUCKETS WITH APPROPRIATE CONCENTRATION TO STORE WET WIPING CLOTHS. PLEASE ENSURE CONTINUED COMPLIANCE.
